lectures.title: Time and Space Complexity of Circular Doubly Linked List

cues.en: All right.
In the last lecture of this section, we are going to look at the big picture of time and space complexity
of circle double linked list.
So I have put over here all methods that we have implemented.
And we have put time and space complexity for them.
Now we have shown you two ways of creating the circle double linked list.
In first way.
We were creating a circle double linked list with one node.
In the second way we are creating an empty circle double linked list.
Now, both constructors have constant time and space complexity because they only involve a few assignments.
Then we have append and prepend method.
Appending and prepending in a double linked list are constant time operations, because they only involve
a few pointers and do not depend on the size of the linked list, then we have insert method.
Now inside insert method, we have used the get method which takes on time complexity and this involves
the traversal to find the insertion point.
So it has a linear time complexity, and the space complexity is constant as it uses a fixed amount
of space then we have over here.
Search method and searching requires visiting each node in the worst case.
So it has a linear time complexity which is going to be on time complexity.
Now the space complexity in this case is O one because no additional space is used that grows with the
input size.
Then we have over here traverse and reverse traversal.
Now we know that in both cases we have to visit each node once.
So that's why it's going to be the linear time complexity.
And they don't use additional space proportional to the input.
So they have a constant space complexity.
Then we have the get method.
The get method returns the node based on the index.
Now, getting an element at a specific index may require traversing the list, leading to the linear
time complexity in the worst case, and the space complexity remains constant.
Now, in the set method, we have used the get method.
So if get method takes on time complexity, it means that set method also will take on time complexity,
because this operation involves the getting the node at a specific index and making its time complexity
linear and space complexity constant.
Then we have pop first and pop methods.
Both methods involve the changing a few pointers and do not depend on the size of the linked list.
That's why they have a constant time and space complexity, because we have a backward reference.
That's why the pop method will take all one time complexity.
But in singly linked list it takes all n time complexity.
Now, when it comes to the remove method, remove operation has a linear time complexity because it
may need to traverse the list to find the node to remove.
Based on their index and the space complexity is constant.
Now the last method is deleting the all nodes, so setting head and tail to the null takes constant
time and does not use any additional space that grows with the size of the list.
That's why the time and space complexity for this method is o one.
So with this we have come to the end of this section.
So in this section we have implemented methods for so-called double linked list.
So hopefully everything is clear.
